messages.author: 37f71d508f34ebb6
messages.subject: CC mice - adding sex as a covariate and CC078
parts:
Hi Dr. Broman, 

Hope you are doing well, I work with the Collaborative Cross (CC) Mice population. I have been using rqtl2 to run some of my data. I got all the files from 
https://github.com/rqtl/qtl2data/blob/master/CC/cc.zip
Thanks for all the preprocessing and example files. 

I have some questions. 

1. I have been averaging  6 animals (3 males and 3 females) from each line to a single data point for the analysis, Is there a way to include sex as a covariate?  (i.e., to run them as CC001M and CC001F, instead of just CC001).
2. The raw data stops at CC076, I have some data from CC078. Is there a way to include the data from CC078 into the analysis ( If its simple enough, I can try to do it myself)? or is there a possibility that it will get added in the future?


I have attached my .josn file. I will appreciate any help on this. 

Thank you,

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: CC mice - adding sex as a covariate and CC078
parts:
Regarding sex as a covariate, personally I would focus on the average of the two sexes and the difference between the sexes.

But if you want to do an analysis with sex as a covariate, you'd need to double the lines with changed names, as you suggest. It'd be particularly important to use an LMM with a kinship matrix, because the pairs CC001M and CC001F have identical genotypes.

There's not currently facilities for doing this double of lines' genotypes in R/qtl2, but I've written some related code for doing individual-level analysis in RILs that might be useful to you:

    https://gist.github.com/kbroman/e09f8116401180b80005d47d4358764f

Regarding the genotypes for CC078: you can try adding it to the existing data at https://github.com/rqtl/qtl2data
You can see the scripts I used to create those data files in https://github.com/rqtl/qtl2data/tree/master/CC/R

I'd like to help folks to analyze CC data in R/qtl2 by making the genotype data available in an easy-to-use format. If you can recommend a source for additional CC data, I'd be happy to hear about it.

karl
